## Proposed change
<!--

The `spc` integration does not retry on startup, so any failures results in a fatal error and the integration doesn't work. The proposed fix ensure that the the call to `async_load_parameters()` is retried (10 times with a retry interval of 2 seconds) before calling it quits.

issue_context.title: SPC component startup timeout
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The `spc` component is very sensitive to timeout on startup and if a single request to its backend fails it will fail and never retry. Perhaps a reasonable way forward would be to retry the call to `async_load_parameters()`  in the startup a couple of times if it fails?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.3.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

spc

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
2022-03-20 18:54:30 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setting up spc
2022-03-20 18:54:41 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of spc is taking over 10 seconds.
2022-03-20 18:54:43 ERROR (MainThread) [pyspcwebgw.utils] Timeout getting SPC data from http://127.0.0.1:8089/spc/zone.
2022-03-20 18:54:49 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.spc] Failed to load area/zone information from SPC
2022-03-20 18:54:49 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain spc took 18.8 seconds
2022-03-20 18:54:49 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup failed for spc: Integration failed to initialize.
```


### Additional information

Related to https://github.com/mbrrg/pyspcwebgw/pull/12

review_comments:
I think it makes more sense to migrate this integration to the UI by implementing a config flow.

The reason for this is that a config entry set up can fail, and Home Assistant will retry set up automatically.
I agree that is a better long term solution. At this point I'm just looking for it to start at all. Would this intermediate fix be acceptable as such?

Nothing more permanent than a temporary solution :)

There are really just 2 configuration parameters to move into the configuration flow, should be fairly straight forward.
